jobs.title: Vice President, Technology Enablement
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **The Klick Group**—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high\-performance, people\-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

**About our Technology Craft**

  

The Technology Craft powers Klick’s platforms, products, and delivery capabilities across healthcare and life sciences. Teams design, build, and operate scalable, secure, and compliant solutions across web, CRM, data, and marketing technologies. By partnering closely with Strategy, Creative, and Client Services, the Technology Craft enables integrated omnichannel experiences that deliver real business impact.

 **Job Description**  

The Vice President, Technology (Technology Enablement) is accountable for the successful delivery of Klick’s core omnichannel technology solutions across a portfolio of healthcare and life sciences clients. Reporting to the SVP of Technology, this role provides portfolio\-level delivery leadership, ensures consistent execution across teams, and builds client confidence in complex, regulated environments. The VP leads through senior Technology Enablement Leads, balancing delivery excellence, operational rigor, and scalable practices as client needs and platforms evolve.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead delivery execution across a multi\-client technology portfolio spanning web platforms, CRM systems, Veeva, and integrated marketing technologies.
* Own end\-to\-end accountability for technology delivery outcomes across Klick\-hosted and client\-managed environments, ensuring adherence to SDLC, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Client Services, Omnichannel Enablement, Strategy, Creative, PMO, and Technology leaders to align delivery plans with business and omnichannel objectives.
* Act as the escalation point for delivery risk, making informed trade\-offs across scope, resourcing, timing, and quality to maintain predictability and client confidence.
* Evolve Klick’s technology delivery operating model by improving governance, forecasting, KPIs, and delivery standards to support scalable, repeatable execution.

  

**Qualifications** **Required:**

* 12\+ years of experience delivering complex enterprise technology solutions, with accountability for large\-scale, multi\-stream delivery programs.
* Demonstrated leadership overseeing omnichannel technology delivery across platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Manager, or comparable enterprise ecosystems.
* Proven experience leading through senior delivery leaders and cross\-functional teams, with clear ownership of outcomes across multiple concurrent initiatives.
* Hands\-on experience with delivery governance frameworks, including SDLC, portfolio planning, risk management, and delivery performance metrics.
* Strong executive communication skills, including translating technical risk and delivery trade\-offs for senior business, IT, and client stakeholders.

**Desired:**

* Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
* Experience delivering technology solutions within US pharmaceutical or healthcare environments, including exposure to regulatory and MLR considerations.
* Agency or consulting background supporting enterprise clients across multiple accounts and delivery models.
* Experience contributing to growth and solution shaping efforts by assessing feasibility, delivery risk, and execution readiness.
* Demonstrated success building and scaling delivery leadership teams while fostering continuous improvement and operational maturity.

  

**Additional Information**  

This posting is to backfill a role at Klick.  

  

\#LI\-TH1 \#LI\-Hybrid

***Our Commitment to Inclusion***  

  

*Klick is consciously creating a culture where everyone can thrive and grow in their careers. We believe that our best work comes from our diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We strongly encourage members of historically underrepresented communities to apply, including Black people, Indigenous peoples, and other people of color, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities and people with intersectional identities. We're also committed to developing an inclusive, barrier\-free recruitment process and work environment. Should you require any accommodation, please contact us at careers@klick.com and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs and ensure you have a positive experience.*

jobs.title: Director of Pricing and Business Analytics
jobs.description:
**About the Role**
==================


GFL is seeking a visionary, high\-energy leader with a passion for financial modeling, advanced analytics, and commercial business insights. Are you a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of complex data, technology, and executive strategy? As the Director of Business Analytics, you will drive our enterprise\-wide intelligence roadmap and foster a high\-impact, data\-driven culture across our fast\-paced, high\-growth organization.


This is a newly created position driven by our consistent expansion, appetite for data\-driven decision\-making, and relentless push for continuous improvement. You will join our leadership team at an exceptionally exciting time as we’ve embarked on our pricing program transformation, placing you at the forefront of this value creating engagement. Working with a "no can't do" attitude, you will translate complex technical data into compelling commercial narratives that shape global corporate strategy and optimize bottom\-line performance.

  

  

**Key Responsibilities**
========================


Reporting directly to the VP, Operations Strategy, you will lead a dynamic team to drive performance and deliver value\-added decision support across the business. Key responsibilities include:

  

  

* **Pricing Excellence:** Assess enterprise pricing performance, build advanced pricing models from scratch, identify margin opportunities, and challenge assumptions. Influence Area Vice Presidents and Business Unit leaders to translate analytical insights into actionable strategies that optimize commercial outcomes.
* **Advanced Analytics \& AI:** Champion statistical modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics to transition the business from descriptive reporting to prescriptive intelligence. Accelerate speed\-to\-insight by integrating modern analytics tools, AWS\-native workflows, predictive machine learning, and responsible GenAI/copilots.
* **Strategic Roadmap Development:** Define and execute the long\-term vision for the Business Analytics department. Scale enterprise data platforms and ensure full alignment between analytics initiatives and global corporate objectives.
* **Operational Excellence:** Oversee the full data lifecycle—from ingestion and pipeline collaboration to the delivery of interactive executive dashboards, automated workflows, and high\-impact predictive tools.
* **Data Governance \& Integrity:** Establish rigorous standards for data quality, security, and governance. Define control frameworks and KPIs to ensure business intelligence is accurate, reliable, and meeting compliance benchmarks.
* **Stakeholder Influence:** Partner closely with Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership. Translate ambiguous operational and market questions into clear recommendations, guiding executive partners through trade\-offs with decision\-ready narratives.
* **Team Leadership:** Hire, coach, and retain a high\-performing team of analysts and data professionals. Foster a culture of continuous improvement, analytical rigor, and collaborative business partnering.
  

  

**Qualifications**
==================


* 10\+ years of progressive experience in analytics, data science, or related quantitative fields, including experimentation frameworks, statistical modeling, and time\-series analysis.
* 5\+ years in pricing, revenue management, or applied data science within B2B or service\-oriented industries, with a proven track record of building dynamic pricing and financial models from scratch.
* 5\+ years of people management experience, including structuring team processes for service delivery in fast\-paced environments, presenting to C\-suite audiences, and driving cross\-functional alignment.
* Expert\-level modeling skills and hands\-on proficiency with major BI tools (Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau) and database querying (SQL).
* Direct experience with AWS cloud data environments (e.g., S3, Glue, Athena, Forecast, or SageMaker) and leveraging GenAI/copilots to accelerate insight generation.
* Executive Communication \& Influence: Exceptional ability to distill complex data insights into concise, persuasive presentations for senior leaders.
* Commercial \& Financial Acumen: Deep understanding of operational finance, FP\&A, and business operations, with the ability to link data metrics directly to bottom\-line profitability.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or Computer Science required; Master’s degree in a quantitative field highly preferred.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Risk Management
jobs.description:
Join one of Canada's fastest\-growing companies and be part of something extraordinary \- welcome to **goeasy**! At goeasy, our people and culture are at the heart of everything we do, and we're proud to be recognized for it. We've earned prestigious accolades such as **Waterstone Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures** and **Canada's Top Growing Companies**. We're also honoured to be named a **Greater Toronto Top Employer** and recognized by **Great Place to Work®** as having the **Best Workplaces for Women** \& **Most Trusted Executive Teams**, and included on **TIME Magazine's 2025 list of Canada's Best Companies**. These honours reflect our commitment to fostering an inclusive, high\-performance culture where talent thrives and innovation drives us forward.


As one of Canada's leading alternative consumer lenders, we're passionate about helping everyday Canadians create a brighter future. Our vision is to provide a path to a better tomorrow, today. We offer a full range of products, including non\-prime leasing, unsecured and secured loans, and point\-of\-sale financing through **easyhome**, **easyfinancial**, and **LendCare**.



If you're seeking an exciting, high\-growth environment where your contributions truly matter, we want to hear from you! Join us, and together, let's create a future of financial empowerment.


**About the Role:**

Reporting directly to the Chief Operations Officer, the **Director, Enterprise Risk Management** will play a pivotal role in building and leading a modern, scalable first\-line risk management function to support goeasy's next stage of growth. This leader will shape the strategy, establish risk management frameworks, and partner with senior executives to identify and manage key non\-credit risks, strengthen operational resilience, and enable smarter, risk\-informed decisions. Leveraging data, technology, AI, and automation, this role will modernize how risk is identified, monitored, and managed, helping the business anticipate challenges, drive operational excellence, and scale with confidence.


**Who You Are:**
----------------



You are a strategic and progressive risk leader who brings a strong combination of business acumen, analytical thinking, and hands\-on execution. You have experience building or evolving risk management frameworks and know how to translate complex risk principles into practical, scalable solutions that drive meaningful business outcomes.



You view risk management as an enabler of growth, not a barrier. You are comfortable challenging conventional thinking, influencing senior stakeholders, and balancing risk mitigation with commercial priorities. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace technology and innovation, and are passionate about building high\-performing teams and fostering a culture of accountability and proactive risk management.


**What You'll Do:**
-------------------


* **Build and lead the function:** Establish and mature a first\-line enterprise risk management function, defining its strategy, operating model, governance, and priorities to support organizational growth.
* **Strengthen risk frameworks:** Develop and implement scalable risk management practices, including risk and control assessments, risk registers, control inventories, issue management, remediation tracking, and executive reporting.
* **Drive enterprise\-wide accountability:** Partner with business leaders to establish clear risk ownership, strengthen internal controls, and embed risk management into day\-to\-day operations and strategic decision\-making.
* **Provide strategic risk advisory:** Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing insights, constructive challenge, and practical recommendations that balance business objectives, customer outcomes, and regulatory expectations.
* **Modernize through technology:** Leverage data analytics, AI, automation, dashboards, and emerging technologies to identify risk trends, monitor key risk indicators, improve controls, and enable proactive decision\-making.
* **Enhance governance and reporting:** Establish effective governance routines, escalation processes, and reporting mechanisms that provide leadership with clear visibility into emerging risks, control effectiveness, and remediation priorities.
* **Build a high\-performing team:** Lead, coach, and develop risk professionals while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

**What You Bring:**
-------------------


* 7\-10 years of progressive experience in enterprise risk management, operational risk, governance, internal controls, compliance, audit, consulting, or related disciplines.
* Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or transforming risk management frameworks, governance structures, control environments, or enterprise\-wide risk programs.
* Strong knowledge of established risk management principles and frameworks, including COSO, the Three Lines Model, risk appetite, risk assessments, control design, monitoring, and remediation.
* Proven experience leading teams or functions across risk management, governance, internal controls, compliance, or operational risk.
* Strong analytical capabilities, with experience leveraging data, KPIs/KRIs, dashboards, automation, AI, or governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms to generate actionable insights.
* Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior executives, challenge constructively, and translate complex risk matters into clear business recommendations.
* Experience within financial services, consumer lending, banking, fintech, insurance, payments, consulting, or another regulated industry is strongly preferred.
* Relevant post\-secondary education or professional designations in risk management, business, finance, audit, compliance, or related fields are considered an asset.

jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**What is the opportunity?**
----------------------------

  

The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture, the RBC Lumina reference architecture and the standards that make data machine\-readable for people, applications and AI agents.


Success means fewer data stores and point\-to\-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

 **What will you do?**

* **Manufacturing (data sources).** Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source.
* **Distribution (RBC Lumina).** Own the Lumina reference architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Run the roadmap to retire point\-to\-point interfaces.
* **Discovery and machine readability.** Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent\-access pattern for data products, such as MCP.
* **Consumption.** Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement\-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
* **Governance by design.** Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support BCBS 239 lineage and jurisdiction\-aware data placement for sovereignty.
* **Simplification and transformation.** Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in\-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third\-party rationalization.

**What do you need to succeed?**
--------------------------------

* 15\+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5\+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
* Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
* A track record of measurable simplification: platforms retired, feeds removed and costs taken out.
* Working knowledge of BCBS 239, privacy regulation and OSFI expectations for data risk.
* Clear view on making data AI\-ready, including retrieval, entitlement propagation and agent access.
* Able to align the CDO, platform engineering and business data owners without direct authority over them.

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Architecture
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**What is the opportunity?**
----------------------------

  

This leader sets one standard way to build, secure and run AI across RBC Technology \& Operations. They own the reference architecture for retrieval\-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, model access and AI\-native software delivery (AI\-DLC). The role turns the 2030 T\&O ambitions, including AI\-native delivery and 30% of GenAI volume on open\-weight models, into patterns teams actually use.


Success means fewer bespoke stacks, faster delivery with maintainable code, and AI that Internal Audit, Model Risk and OSFI can trust.

**What will you do****?**
-------------------------

* **AI architecture standards as code.** Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.
* **Common RAG substrate.** Converge the many RAG solutions onto one shared platform: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and evaluation. Retrieval must respect source entitlements by default. Set a retirement plan for duplicate stacks.
* **Agent sandboxing and security architecture.** Design the sandbox standard for every agentic workload: ephemeral environments, egress allow\-lists, short\-lived task\-scoped credentials and no standing production access. Own agent identity, tool access through a governed MCP gateway and registry, and defenses against prompt injection and poisoned tools.
* **AI\-DLC harness and quality gates.** Own the harness architecture from spec to release. Make quality gates deterministic and mandatory: tests and coverage, static analysis, complexity and duplication limits, dependency and license checks, security scanning and architecture fitness checks. Enforce separation of duties (the agent that writes a change cannot approve it), PR size limits and traceability from spec to deployment.
* **Skills and evaluation lifecycle.** Treat skills like code: owned, versioned, regression\-tested with evals and retired when stale. Re\-run evals before any model upgrade reaches teams.
* **Model gateway and inference architecture.** Route work across frontier and open\-weight models by cost, risk and jurisdiction. Build in token metering, caching and data\-classification rules so cost and residency are enforced by the platform.
* **Risk\-tiered control model.** Partner with Internal Audit, Model Risk and Cyber to define human\-oversight tiers, from human\-on\-the\-loop for low\-risk work to human\-in\-the\-loop for payments and core banking. Align with OSFI Guidelines E\-23 and B\-13\.
* **Design authority and innovation.** Chair AI architecture review, keep decision records and manage exceptions. Graduate proven lab work into the platform and evaluate emerging technology, such as agent protocols and new open\-weight models.

**What do you need to succeed?**
--------------------------------

* 15\+ years in architecture or engineering, including 5\+ years leading architects or engineers at enterprise scale.
* Hands\-on depth in LLM systems: RAG, agent frameworks, MCP, evaluation and inference serving on cloud and on\-premises GPUs.
* Security architecture for AI, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, sandboxing and identity for non\-human actors.
* Strong DevSecOps and SDLC background; you have shipped quality gates engineers accepted rather than routed around.
* Experience in a regulated industry, ideally financial services under OSFI.
* Credibility with engineers: you still prototype and read code. Able to explain trade\-offs plainly to executives and audit.

 **What’s in it for you?**

**Job Summary**

The Executive Assistant (“EA”) plays an important role in supporting the Chief Technology, Data \& AI Officer (CTDAIO) and the day\-to\-day operations of the Information Technology Division. Reporting directly to the CTDAIO, the EA provides proactive administrative and operational support and works closely with the IT leadership team.  



  

This role goes beyond day\-to\-day executive support. The EA will help the CTDAIO stay organized and focused across priorities related to technology, data, AI, cybersecurity, talent, and transformation. The successful candidate will anticipate what is needed, take ownership, use good judgment, and follow through on decisions and commitments.  

  



**What you will do:**

  

**Note:** This role is required to work in the office full\-time.  

  



Executive \& Divisional Support


* Provide administrative support to the CTDAIO, including calendar management, meeting coordination, travel arrangements, correspondence, and preparation for executive, Board, committee, and divisional commitments.
* Manage competing priorities and use good judgment to protect the CTDAIO’s time and keep attention focused on the most important issues.
* Anticipate deadlines, decisions, dependencies, and potential issues; address what can be resolved independently and raise matters that require the CTDAIO’s attention.
* Work with the IT leadership team and partners across the organization to clarify owners, actions, and timelines and follow up on commitments.

Prepare clear, accurate, and well\-formatted materials to support decision\-making.  

* 

Leadership Meetings \& Follow\-Through


* Support the CTDAIO’s executive, Board, committee, and IT leadership responsibilities by coordinating schedules, agendas, materials, pre\-reads, decisions, and follow\-up.
* Prepare and circulate meeting notes when needed, clearly capturing decisions, owners, timelines, and dependencies.
* Track priorities and commitments, follow up to keep work moving, and flag items that are delayed or at risk.
* Maintain executive and governance records in line with confidentiality, audit, and documentation requirements.

Work closely with Executive Assistants, committee secretaries, and partners across the organization to coordinate schedules, materials, and follow\-up.  

* 

Expense and Administrative Support


* Process invoices, expense claims, purchase documentation, and payments accurately and on time.

Track deadlines and follow up on missing information or approvals to keep administrative work on schedule.

Our client is a fast\-growing developer, owner and operator of community solar, distributed generation and energy storage assets in the US. Reporting to the CFO, you will build and execute the financing strategies that fund the company's next stage of growth.  

  



**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital markets and capital formation**

* Develop and execute the capital markets strategy with the CFO, CEO and executive leadership team.
* Lead capital raising across project, portfolio, asset and corporate financing structures.
* Evaluate and execute financing options, including:
	+ Construction debt
	+ Term debt and back\-leverage facilities
	+ Tax equity and tax credit transfers
	+ Preferred equity and growth equity
	+ Corporate debt and revolving credit facilities
	+ Joint ventures and portfolio financings
	+ Structured capital solutions and asset\-level refinancing
	+ Other strategic financing arrangements

* Lead negotiations with commercial banks, institutional investors, infrastructure funds, tax equity providers, private credit providers, investment banks, rating agencies and other capital partners.
* Run financing processes end to end: market engagement, term sheets, diligence, documentation, closing and post\-closing compliance.

* Track capital markets conditions, interest rates, lender requirements, tax equity availability, investor appetite and renewable energy financing trends.

### **Project and portfolio capitalisation strategy**

* Set up a disciplined process for deciding which projects and portfolios to prioritise for capitalisation.

* Build and maintain a prioritised capitalisation roadmap for the development pipeline and operating portfolio.
* Recommend the best timing, structure and grouping of projects for financing.
* Decide whether projects are financed individually, aggregated into portfolios, placed in warehouse facilities, contributed to joint ventures or funded with corporate capital.
* Weigh how to deploy limited capital across community solar, commercial and industrial solar, standalone storage and hybrid solar\-plus\-storage.
* Identify capital constraints, concentration risks, funding gaps and dependencies that could affect construction schedules or commercial operation dates.
* Recommend corrective actions or alternative structures when projects fall short of capitalisation requirements.
* Monitor capitalised projects against underwriting assumptions, financing milestones, budgets and expected returns.

### **Project underwriting and investment analysis**

* Lead financial underwriting for community solar, distributed generation, energy storage and related investments.

**Job Description**

**What is the opportunity?**
----------------------------

  

The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture, the RBC Lumina reference architecture and the standards that make data machine\-readable for people, applications and AI agents.


Success means fewer data stores and point\-to\-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

 **What will you do?**

* **Manufacturing (data sources).** Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source.
* **Distribution (RBC Lumina).** Own the Lumina reference architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Run the roadmap to retire point\-to\-point interfaces.
* **Discovery and machine readability.** Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent\-access pattern for data products, such as MCP.
* **Consumption.** Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement\-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
* **Governance by design.** Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support BCBS 239 lineage and jurisdiction\-aware data placement for sovereignty.
* **Simplification and transformation.** Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in\-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third\-party rationalization.

**Job Description**

**What is the opportunity?**
----------------------------

  

This leader sets one standard way to build, secure and run AI across RBC Technology \& Operations. They own the reference architecture for retrieval\-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, model access and AI\-native software delivery (AI\-DLC). The role turns the 2030 T\&O ambitions, including AI\-native delivery and 30% of GenAI volume on open\-weight models, into patterns teams actually use.


Success means fewer bespoke stacks, faster delivery with maintainable code, and AI that Internal Audit, Model Risk and OSFI can trust.

**What will you do****?**
-------------------------

* **AI architecture standards as code.** Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.
* **Common RAG substrate.** Converge the many RAG solutions onto one shared platform: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and evaluation. Retrieval must respect source entitlements by default. Set a retirement plan for duplicate stacks.
* **Agent sandboxing and security architecture.** Design the sandbox standard for every agentic workload: ephemeral environments, egress allow\-lists, short\-lived task\-scoped credentials and no standing production access. Own agent identity, tool access through a governed MCP gateway and registry, and defenses against prompt injection and poisoned tools.
* **AI\-DLC harness and quality gates.** Own the harness architecture from spec to release. Make quality gates deterministic and mandatory: tests and coverage, static analysis, complexity and duplication limits, dependency and license checks, security scanning and architecture fitness checks. Enforce separation of duties (the agent that writes a change cannot approve it), PR size limits and traceability from spec to deployment.
* **Skills and evaluation lifecycle.** Treat skills like code: owned, versioned, regression\-tested with evals and retired when stale. Re\-run evals before any model upgrade reaches teams.
* **Model gateway and inference architecture.** Route work across frontier and open\-weight models by cost, risk and jurisdiction. Build in token metering, caching and data\-classification rules so cost and residency are enforced by the platform.
* **Risk\-tiered control model.** Partner with Internal Audit, Model Risk and Cyber to define human\-oversight tiers, from human\-on\-the\-loop for low\-risk work to human\-in\-the\-loop for payments and core banking. Align with OSFI Guidelines E\-23 and B\-13\.
* **Design authority and innovation.** Chair AI architecture review, keep decision records and manage exceptions. Graduate proven lab work into the platform and evaluate emerging technology, such as agent protocols and new open\-weight models.

**What do you need to succeed?**
--------------------------------

* 15\+ years in architecture or engineering, including 5\+ years leading architects or engineers at enterprise scale.
* Hands\-on depth in LLM systems: RAG, agent frameworks, MCP, evaluation and inference serving on cloud and on\-premises GPUs.
* Security architecture for AI, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, sandboxing and identity for non\-human actors.
* Strong DevSecOps and SDLC background; you have shipped quality gates engineers accepted rather than routed around.
* Experience in a regulated industry, ideally financial services under OSFI.
* Credibility with engineers: you still prototype and read code. Able to explain trade\-offs plainly to executives and audit.

**Overview**
------------

Our client is a fast\-growing developer, owner and operator of community solar, distributed generation and energy storage assets in the US. They are hiring a Senior Vice President to lead capital formation, structured finance, investment underwriting, capital allocation and financial planning.  

  



Reporting to the CFO, you will build and execute the financing strategies that fund the company's next stage of growth.  

  



**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital markets and capital formation**

* Develop and execute the capital markets strategy with the CFO, CEO and executive leadership team.
* Lead capital raising across project, portfolio, asset and corporate financing structures.
* Evaluate and execute financing options, including:
	+ Construction debt
	+ Term debt and back\-leverage facilities
	+ Tax equity and tax credit transfers
	+ Preferred equity and growth equity
	+ Corporate debt and revolving credit facilities
	+ Joint ventures and portfolio financings
	+ Structured capital solutions and asset\-level refinancing
	+ Other strategic financing arrangements
* Build financing strategies that balance cost of capital, liquidity, execution certainty, covenants, risk allocation and long\-term enterprise value.
* Lead negotiations with commercial banks, institutional investors, infrastructure funds, tax equity providers, private credit providers, investment banks, rating agencies and other capital partners.
* Run financing processes end to end: market engagement, term sheets, diligence, documentation, closing and post\-closing compliance.
* Maintain relationships with existing capital providers and open up new sources of institutional capital.
* Track capital markets conditions, interest rates, lender requirements, tax equity availability, investor appetite and renewable energy financing trends.
* Recommend when to finance, refinance, hold, sell, aggregate or otherwise monetise individual assets and portfolios.

### **Project and portfolio capitalisation strategy**

* Set up a disciplined process for deciding which projects and portfolios to prioritise for capitalisation.
* Assess projects on development maturity, interconnection status, permitting, site control, subscriber readiness, offtake, revenue certainty, construction needs, tax credit eligibility, financing availability and projected returns.
* Work with Development, Project Finance, EPC, Asset Management, Subscriber Management, Legal, Tax, Accounting and Operations to judge project readiness and financing risk.
* Build and maintain a prioritised capitalisation roadmap for the development pipeline and operating portfolio.
* Recommend the best timing, structure and grouping of projects for financing.
* Decide whether projects are financed individually, aggregated into portfolios, placed in warehouse facilities, contributed to joint ventures or funded with corporate capital.
* Weigh how to deploy limited capital across community solar, commercial and industrial solar, standalone storage and hybrid solar\-plus\-storage.
* Identify capital constraints, concentration risks, funding gaps and dependencies that could affect construction schedules or commercial operation dates.
* Recommend corrective actions or alternative structures when projects fall short of capitalisation requirements.
* Monitor capitalised projects against underwriting assumptions, financing milestones, budgets and expected returns.

### **Project underwriting and investment analysis**

* Lead financial underwriting for community solar, distributed generation, energy storage and related investments.
* Set consistent underwriting standards, investment criteria, risk classifications and minimum return thresholds.
* Evaluate project and portfolio economics, including:
	+ Development, construction, interconnection and operating costs
	+ Generation and production assumptions
	+ Subscriber acquisition and management costs
	+ PPA terms and community solar credit values
	+ Renewable energy incentives, Investment Tax Credits and adders
	+ Debt sizing and tax equity economics
	+ Merchant versus contracted revenue exposure
	+ Residual and terminal value
* Assess risks across development, interconnection, permitting, construction, supply chain, revenue, customer concentration, regulation, financing conditions and operating performance.
* Make sure investment recommendations combine quantitative analysis with a grounded view of execution risk.
* Own underwriting templates, approval thresholds, risk methodologies and investment review procedures.
* Compare actual project and portfolio performance with original underwriting, explain variances and recommend corrective action.
* Feed lessons from operating assets and completed financings back into underwriting standards.

### **Financial modelling and sensitivity analysis**

* Provide executive oversight of project, portfolio, financing and enterprise financial models.
* Personally review, modify and challenge complex models, rather than relying on outputs alone.
* Use models to test alternative capital structures, financing terms, project groupings, development schedules and operating assumptions.
* Run sensitivity, scenario and downside analysis on capital costs, interest rates, debt capacity, tax equity terms, tax credit eligibility, construction costs, production, subscriber performance, revenue rates, operating expenses, delays, refinancing and exit values.
* Evaluate IRR, NPV, ROIC, cash yield, debt\-service coverage, leverage and payback.
* Keep models accurate, transparent, auditable and aligned with approved corporate assumptions.
* Set model governance: version control, review standards, ownership and approval protocols.
